physical_harm: Death caused by strangulation; rape committed multiple times
premeditation_planning: The court found the crime was premeditated and planned
key_evidence_accepted: The court accepted the evidence of PW8, who witnessed the accused having sexual intercourse with the minor girl, and the medical evidence indicating the cause of death was asphyxia due to strangulation. The court also relied on the circumstantial evidence and the last seen theory established by the prosecution.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of PW8 as crucial and found no reason to doubt his testimony, noting he had no enmity or grudge against the accused and could easily identify him. The court also found the medical evidence credible and corroborated by other witnesses.
trial_duration: Trial court convicted accused No.1 u/ss. 302, 376, 366-A, 363 r/w. s.34 IPC and sentenced him to death u/s. 302 IPC alongwith punishment for other offences. Accused No.2 was convicted for the offences punishable u/s.363A r/w. s. 34 IPC and was sentenced to 5 years RI. Accused No.1 preferred appeal before High Court, which was dismissed and his death sentence was confirmed. Hence the present appeal. Dismissing the appeal, and converting the death sentence to life imprisonment
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court not stated
investigation_status: The police after booking the accused for offence u/s. 377 IPC failed to charge sheet him, in spite of the fact the medical evidence had clearly established the commission of carnal intercourse on a minor girl with moderate intellectual disability.
procedural_irregularity: Non-reporting of sexual assault on minor children is a disturbing trend in our society, which has happened in the present case as well. PW-8 though was witness to the crime he did not report the said fact to the police
appeal_history: Appeal dismissed by High Court and confirmed death sentence. Appeal dismissed by Supreme Court and converted death sentence to life imprisonment
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused, aged about 52 years, committed the rape and murder of a minor and intellectually challenged girl, and that the guilt of the accused was proved beyond reasonable doubt. The trial court and High Court correctly appreciated the evidence and documents adduced, finding that the guilt of the accused was proved beyond reasonable doubt.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused is having two sons aged 26 and 27 years and are dependent on him, which is not a mitigating circumstance. The accused was an able bodied person and was the father of two children, and reformation or rehabilitation is practically ruled out.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the 'crime test', 'criminal test', and the 'rarest of rare test' while awarding the death sentence. The 'crime test' requires the crime to be of the utmost gravity, the 'criminal test' requires no mitigating circumstances, and the 'rarest of rare test' is society-centric and not judge-centric.

sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the crime was of the utmost gravity, the accused was not a menace to society, and reformation or rehabilitation is practically ruled out. The 'rarest of rare test' was applied, which is society-centric and not judge-centric, and the death sentence was converted to life imprisonment.
judicial_aggravating_factors: The accused was aged 52 years, the victim was an 11-year-old minor with moderate intellectual disability, and the crime was inhuman and barbaric. The accused repeatedly raped the girl for several days and then strangulated her to death.
other_sentence_order: All the sentences awarded, including life imprisonment and other sentences, are directed to run consecutively.
